content: He is known as Khwāja Turka Iṣfahānī or Ṣāʾin-i Turka; the short form Ibn Turka is used to distinguish him as the most eminent of the line. Full name (note 1): Ṣāʾin al-Dīn Abū Muḥammad ʿAlī b. Afżal al-Dīn Muḥammad b. Ṣadr al-Dīn Abī Ḥāmid Muḥammad Turka Iṣfahānī Khujandī. He uses the takhalluṣ ʿAlī in his small surviving poetry and usually signs letters Ṣāyin-i Turka. The honorific Ṣāʾin al-Dīn is sometimes wrongly given as Żiyāʾ al-Dīn in the sources.
